Check a supplement site before a release

Source: R/check-supplement.R
check_supplement.Rd

check_supplement() looks for problems that can break a release of a site, publish files that must stay private, or publish the template's placeholder values in place of the author's. It changes no file. It prints each problem it finds and returns all of them as a data frame.

Usage

check_supplement(path = ".")

Arguments

path

The folder of the site.

Value

A data frame with one row per problem and the character columns check, file (the path in the site), and problem, invisibly. It has zero rows when the function finds no problem. Its skipped attribute names the git checks ("large-file", "saved-object", and "ignored-output") that did not run, and is empty when they ran.

Details

The checks, by the value in the check column:

  • "large-file": a file larger than 100 MiB (104,857,600 bytes), which GitHub refuses. A symbolic link, or on Windows a junction, is not counted, because git stores only the link.

  • "saved-object": a saved R object (.rds, .rda, .rdata, .qs, or .qs2, in any letter case). A fitted model saved this way can hold the data it was fitted to.

  • "ignored-output": a file that git ignores in figures/, docs/, or _freeze/, so that a release leaves it out of the published site. The check takes each regular file in these folders, and in the folders in them, that is reached without passing through a symbolic link or, on Windows, a junction, and whose path holds no name that starts with .. The file gets a row when git neither tracks it nor lists it as untracked, because its ignore rules exclude it, such as a rule in .gitignore or .git/info/exclude. A file that git tracks gives no row, also when a rule matches it. The copy of a data file in docs/data/ gets a row when a rule also matches the copy, as the template's rule for .rds files does. The problem text says to change the rule for a file that the site must publish, and to remove the source of a private file and render again.

  • "no-stored-output": a .qmd report directly in analyses/, not in a folder inside it, with code and no stored output in _freeze/. A full render then runs its code, which needs the data. A report has code when a line starts a code chunk: any mix of spaces, tabs, and > characters, three or more backticks, optional spaces or tabs, then { and a name. The name is the longest run of an ASCII letter followed by ASCII letters, digits, _, or .. Any text without } can follow the name, then }, and the line ends with optional spaces or tabs. A chunk named ojs, mermaid, or dot, in any letter case, does not count, because Quarto starts no engine for it. Every other name counts, such as {bash} or {sql}, and so does a chunk in a report whose front matter sets engine: markdown. Quarto also reads other white space, line breaks included, between the backticks and { and after }. It lets the text after the name run across lines, and it starts a line after U+2028 or U+2029. Such chunk starts are not found. A nul byte in a report counts as a character that is none of those this rule names. A report with no chunk that counts also has code when it has inline R code on one line and the top-level engine in its own front matter is knitr. Inline R code is a backtick, then r and a space or #, or {r} and a space, then text with no backtick, then a backtick. Inline code that spans lines is not found, nor is inline code with a tab after {r}, which knitr also runs. Nor is knitr that a knitr key, execute: engine, an included file, or _metadata.yml turns on. A report has no stored output when _freeze/analyses/<name>/execute-results/ holds no file other than hidden files and the files in hidden folders.

  • "stale-output": a .qmd report directly in analyses/, from the same list of reports, whose stored output was made from other text than the report holds now. The check reads as JSON each file whose name ends in .json and does not start with ., directly in _freeze/analyses/<name>/execute-results/. Quarto writes the MD5 of the report's text there as the top-level hash. The report gets one row when such a hash is one text value that differs from the MD5 of the report's bytes with each CR LF pair read as LF. It also gets one row, which says that the source hash of its stored output cannot be read, when such a file does not parse, its top level is not an object, or its top-level hash is missing or is not one text value. When one file cannot be read and another differs, the one row has this text. A report that cannot be read, such as a link to a missing file, gives no row. Quarto 1.10.19 hashes only the report file, so a change in a file that the report includes, in _quarto.yml or _metadata.yml, or in the data gives no row. Reports in folders inside analyses/ are not read. Quarto reads a report as UTF-8 and hashes each byte that is not valid UTF-8 as U+FFFD, so such a report gets a row after each render. The row names, by their paths from the site folder in byte order, each of these files whose hash differs, or in the "cannot be read" text only each file whose hash cannot be read. Each path stands between double quotes, with a \ before each \ and " in it, so that a name that holds a comma and a space reads as one file. The "cannot be read" text ends with the render steps and then a delete step. It says that if the row stays after the render steps, the files can be from a format that the report no longer renders, or damaged. Then it says to delete them, render the whole site, and commit the report with _freeze/, docs/, and figures/. Quarto keeps the file of a format that the report no longer renders, such as docx.json, with its old hash. So when every hash can be read and another of these files has a hash equal to that MD5 of the report, the row also says that the files that differ can be from a format that the report no longer renders. If so, delete them, render the whole site, and commit the report with _freeze/, docs/, and figures/. If not, follow the render steps that the row gives after the hint.

  • "leftover-output": a folder directly in _freeze/analyses/, whose name does not start with ., that no file or folder in analyses/ names. A name in analyses/ names the folder when, cut before its last . (the whole name when it holds no .), it equals the folder's name with letter case ignored: the case of ASCII letters always, and the case of other letters as tolower() reads it in the session's locale. In a name that is not valid UTF-8, only the case of ASCII letters is ignored. A name stored in another Unicode form, composed or decomposed, does not match. Quarto 1.10.19 keeps a report's folder after the report is deleted or renamed. The row says to delete the folder, render the whole site, and commit _freeze/ and docs/, and for a deleted or renamed report also its old path and _quarto.yml. Folders inside subfolders of _freeze/analyses/ and folders directly in _freeze/ are not read. A file or folder in analyses/ of the same name, such as <name>.R, hides a leftover folder. So does a report whose name differs only in letter case, as after a report is renamed only in letter case on Linux.

  • "not-rendered": the site has no docs/ folder.

  • "broken-link": an href, src, or xlink:href link on a page in docs/ to a file that is not in docs/, or to a folder there with no index.html, or a link that ends with / to a file. A page that cannot be read, such as a link to a missing file, also counts. Pages in every folder of docs/ are read, hidden files and folders (names that start with .) included. A symbolic link to a folder, or on Windows a junction, is not entered. A page in a folder that such a link points to is read once, at its own path, when the folder is in docs/. A symbolic link in docs/ to a page file in docs/ is read as a page of its own. A symbolic link or junction in docs/ whose target exists and resolves to a place outside docs/ gives a row of its own, because the published site does not have its target. So a link to such a link also gives a row. A page that it points to, or a page in a folder that it points to, is not read. A link on a page whose path passes through or ends at such a link also counts. For a link to a folder, the folder's index.html is part of that path. A symbolic link or junction that resolves to docs/ or a place in it gives no row of its own. Links that start with /, #, or a scheme such as https: are not checked, and no web address is requested. GitHub Pages matches letter case, so a link whose case differs from the file name counts as broken, also on a disk that ignores case. A link that also differs from the name in Unicode form (for example é written as e plus an accent) is not caught.

    Links are read from start tags only, as a browser reads them. Comments, <!...> and <?...> markup, and the text of <script>, <style>, <textarea>, and <title> elements are skipped, and so is page text such as <code> text. Attribute names match in any letter case, and only whole names count, so data-href and data-src are not read. A value can be in double quotes, in single quotes, or unquoted, where it runs to the next space or >. An attribute with no =, such as <a href>, has an empty value and is not checked. A start tag that the end of the page cuts off is not read, as a browser drops it. A page whose markup goes past the limits of the PCRE pattern engine gives one row that says so, in place of its link rows. Such a page holds millions of - in one comment, millions of < in the text of one script, style, textarea, or title element (about 5 million did, in a page of 20 MB), or millions of attributes in one tag. Each value is handled in this order: character references are decoded; spaces, tabs, line breaks, and form feeds at its ends are removed and tabs and line breaks inside it are dropped; links with a scheme, /, or # at the start are skipped; then % escapes are decoded. The decoded references are &amp;, &lt;, &gt;, &quot;, and &apos; (in lower case, with the ;), and number references such as &#38; or &#x26; with the ; that name a code point from 1 to 0x10FFFF, other than a surrogate or 128 to 159. A row shows the link after the references are decoded, the ends removed, and the tabs and line breaks inside it dropped.

    These are the main cases where the check reads a page differently from a browser. Every other reference (such as &eacute;, &AMP;, or &#38 with no ;) stays as written. Other control characters at the ends of a link, such as &#1;, stay, while a browser removes them. The text of <noscript>, <xmp>, <iframe>, <noembed>, <noframes>, and <plaintext> elements is read as markup, and so is the text of a <![CDATA[...]]> section after its first >. The four skipped elements are also skipped inside <svg> and <math>. A comment ends only at the first -->, so <!--> and <!---> also run to the next -->, and --!> does not end it. A script ends at its first </script>, also when its text holds <!-- and <script>, where a browser reads on to a later </script>. A " or ' with no closing quote starts an unquoted value, so the next > ends that tag and it is read, where a browser reads on to the end of the page and drops the tag. A byte that is not valid UTF-8 is read as text such as <e9>; outside a quoted value, its > ends the tag, so an unquoted value keeps the <e9 part and the later attributes of that tag are not read. A second attribute of the same name is also read.

  • "unpublished-figure": a paper figure that the last render did not copy into docs/. The check takes each regular file in figures/, and in the folders in it, that is reached without passing through a symbolic link or junction, and whose path holds no name that starts with .. The file gets a row when the same path under docs/figures/ is not a regular file, or when the MD5 of its bytes differs. A render copies into docs/figures/ the files that figures/ holds when the render starts, so a figure saved under a new name or changed after the last render gets a row, and a full render or a render of a report by name clears it. Hidden files are not compared, though Quarto copies them too.

  • "doi-mismatch": the DOI in CITATION.cff differs from the one that write_citation() writes from _supplement.yml, or the DOI badge on docs/index.html differs from zenodo.version-doi (or zenodo.concept-doi when that is empty). A home page whose source uses {{< supplement-doi >}} but that shows no badge, while _supplement.yml has a DOI, also counts. So does a CITATION.cff that cannot be read or is not a YAML map (a link to a missing file included), and a DOI in CITATION.cff or on the badge that is not a DOI.

  • "placeholder": a template value that the author has not replaced, so that a release would archive it. The check compares the site with the template that the installed package holds:

    • _supplement.yml gets one row when paper-title, citation, or contact equals the template's value, or an authors entry has the family and given of a template author. Values are compared with each run of white space read as one space and the ends removed. A value that is not one text value does not count. The row names the fields.

    • _quarto.yml gets a row for the line href: https://github.com/OWNER/REPO, index.qmd for the line ## Before your first commit, LICENSE.md and LICENSE-CC-BY.md for the line Copyright (c) YEAR AUTHORS, and README.md, SUPPLEMENT.md, and _README.md for the line Website: https://OWNER.github.io/REPO/. SUPPLEMENT.md is for a site made before the template's guide moved to GUIDE.md: when that site's first render found a README.md, it wrote the guide to SUPPLEMENT.md. Spaces, tabs, and a carriage return at the ends of a line are ignored. A file that is missing, a folder, not UTF-8 text, or that cannot be read gives no row.

    • analyses/example.qmd and data/example.csv each get a row when their text equals the template's copy, with each CR LF read as LF. A file that cannot be read gives no row.

    Only a whole value or a whole line counts, so a value that keeps part of a placeholder, such as a citation with (Year) in it, gives no row. A site made from an older version of the template, whose placeholders differ from the installed ones, gives no row for them.

The "large-file" and "saved-object" checks look at the files that git tracks or does not ignore, which git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard lists, so files that .gitignore blocks are left out. The "ignored-output" check reads the files that git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard lists in figures/, docs/, and _freeze/. For these three git checks the function runs git only to read: git --version, git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree, and git ls-files. When git is not on the PATH, one of these commands fails, or the folder is not in a git work tree, it skips these three checks and says so.

Errors

The function stops with an error of class supplement_error and one of these classes:

  • supplement_error_argument: path is not a single non-empty string.

  • supplement_error_no_metadata: path holds no _supplement.yml.

  • supplement_error_parse: the yaml package cannot read _supplement.yml, as for write_citation().

  • supplement_error_no_map: _supplement.yml has no supplement: map.

  • supplement_error_field_type: a DOI in _supplement.yml is not one text value, or zenodo is not a map.

  • supplement_error_doi: a DOI in _supplement.yml is not a DOI.

See also

write_citation() to write CITATION.cff again.

Examples

site <- file.path(tempdir(), "check-example")
create_supplement(site)
#> ✔ Made a supplement site in /tmp/Rtmpv6D8NQ/check-example.
#> ℹ Replace `OWNER/REPO` in _quarto.yml, and `OWNER` and `REPO` in the site
#>   address in _README.md, with your GitHub repository.
#> ℹ Put the paper facts in _supplement.yml.
#> ℹ Run `quarto render` in /tmp/Rtmpv6D8NQ/check-example once before your first
#>   commit.
# A new site has not been rendered, its example report has no stored
# output yet, and it still holds the template's placeholder values.
problems <- check_supplement(site)
#> ℹ Skipped the "large-file", "saved-object", and "ignored-output" checks: `git rev-parse` failed, or the folder is not in a git work tree.
#> ✖ 11 problems found in /tmp/Rtmpv6D8NQ/check-example:
#> ✖ no-stored-output analyses/example.qmd: The report has code and no stored
#>   output in _freeze/. Render the report by name, render the whole site, then
#>   commit the report with _freeze/, docs/, and figures/. If you added the report
#>   to the Analyses menu, as add_report() does, also commit _quarto.yml.
#> ✖ not-rendered docs: The site has no docs/ folder. Render the site.
#> ✖ unpublished-figure figures/bootstrap-means.png: The copy in docs/figures/ is
#>   missing or differs. Render the whole site, then commit figures/, docs/, and
#>   _freeze/.
#> ✖ placeholder _supplement.yml: Template values left in place: paper-title,
#>   citation, contact, authors. Replace them before a release.
#> ✖ placeholder _quarto.yml: The GitHub link names OWNER/REPO. Write your GitHub
#>   repository in its place.
#> ✖ placeholder index.qmd: The "Before your first commit" box is still on the
#>   home page. Delete it.
#> ✖ placeholder LICENSE.md: The copyright line reads YEAR AUTHORS. Write the year
#>   and the authors in its place.
#> ✖ placeholder LICENSE-CC-BY.md: The copyright line reads YEAR AUTHORS. Write
#>   the year and the authors in its place.
#> ✖ placeholder _README.md: The site address names OWNER and REPO. Write your
#>   GitHub account and repository in their place.
#> ✖ placeholder analyses/example.qmd: This is the template's example report.
#>   Write your own report in it, or delete it and its stored output in
#>   _freeze/analyses/example/, and make the Analyses menu in _quarto.yml list
#>   your own reports.
#> ✖ placeholder data/example.csv: This is the template's example data. Put your
#>   own data in it, or delete it, its entry under data in _supplement.yml, and
#>   the example report, which reads it.
problems$check
#>  [1] "no-stored-output"   "not-rendered"       "unpublished-figure"
#>  [4] "placeholder"        "placeholder"        "placeholder"       
#>  [7] "placeholder"        "placeholder"        "placeholder"       
#> [10] "placeholder"        "placeholder"       
unlink(site, recursive = TRUE)
